title: Tourism service supply chains in ten emerging economies: data collection, audited analysis and validation notebooks
description:
Versioned computational materials for a study of reported disruption exposure and customer impact in tourism service supply chains across ten emerging economies. The frozen analytical run contains 51,037 reviews from 11,500 providers in 29 cities.

Contents. The deposit includes a dry-run collection notebook documenting the Google Places retrieval protocol; an audited analysis notebook implementing exclusions, frozen dictionary coding, supplier-clustered logistic models, Firth rare-events checks, Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction, TOST equivalence tests, restricted-sample robustness, leave-one-out same-source assessment, country heterogeneity and publication figures; aggregate reference tables T0–T12 with a reproducibility manifest; and, new in this version, three companion notebooks that define the held-out validation procedure.

Data availability. No review-level platform content is distributed. Review text, reviewer display names, ratings and related Places content are excluded from the deposit. The public materials comprise the computational method and aggregate non-identifying reference outputs. Re-execution on a newly retrieved relevance-ranked platform sample is not expected to reproduce the frozen corpus exactly.

Measurement scope. The public version documents dictionary diagnostics, rule-based text indicators and the validation procedure: how the held-out double-coded sample is drawn, which agreement statistics are computed on returned codings, how the provider query-stratum audit is scored, and how a gold-labelled train/validation/test split is built without provider leakage. Only the procedure is deposited. Individual human-coding records, provider-audit records and the resulting validation metrics are outside the scope of this public release and are not contained in it; the notebooks read inputs that are not distributed here and produce no output without them.

Provider strata. The provider grouping used in the analysis records which retrieval query returned each provider; it is not a verified organizational characteristic of the firm. The validation materials therefore name it a query stratum — mass-market versus creative-tourism — and results are read as patterns associated with the retrieval strategy rather than as properties of the providers. An earlier audit that asked an independent assessor to recover an organizational typology from the same label returned chance-level agreement; that negative result is documented in the validation materials as a limit of the proxy.

notes: Version 1.3.0 narrows the coding instruction for the labour construct, named WorkforceLanguage in the accompanying manuscript. Held-out double coding by two independent coders gave inter-rater agreement of 0.85 on this construct against 0.33 and 0.34 with the dictionary: both coders read bare service-role mentions (guide, driver, receptionist) as workforce references, whereas the dictionary implements the narrower reading of explicit workforce, staffing, training and professionalism discourse, and role mentions are already captured by the chain-stage indicators. The instruction now states the narrow definition. Dictionary patterns, column names and reference outputs are unchanged. Add the article DOI as a related identifier once the article is published.
